extracted.intended_audience: general readers and those interested in humor, folklore, and gender/stereotype studies
extracted.subtask_description: Describing the defining features, variants, and criticisms of the 'blonde joke' cycle — jokes that rely on a stereotype of a 'dumb blonde' woman. Explains common formats, themes, meta-jokes, and social critiques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stereotype basis / target of joke
rubrics_metrics.description: Blonde jokes are a joke cycle based on a stereotype of a dumb blonde woman. The target is generally people (usually women) who have blonde hair; they serve as a form of blonde versus brunette rivalry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These jokes rely explicitly on hair-color stereotyping to generate humor; note that many are mere variants on traditional ethnic or group-based jokes and are often considered derogatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical format: situation highlighting promiscuity or lack of intelligence
rubrics_metrics.description: Blonde jokes nearly always take the format of the blonde placing herself in a situation or making a comment that serves to highlight her supposed promiscuity and/or lack of intelligence, cluelessness and clumsiness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A typical plot places the blonde in an unusual situation (often contrasted with a brunette or redhead) so her words or actions underscore the stereotype. Example provided: a long ventriloquist meta-joke where the blonde's protests end with a punch line that reinforces her supposed stupidity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of sexual humour
rubrics_metrics.description: Some blonde jokes rely on sexual humour to portray or stereotype their subjects as promiscuous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sexualization is a common theme and contributes to the jokes' offensiveness; such content often overlaps with portrayals of sexual promiscuity as evidence of stupidity or lack of moral character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison/contrast with other hair-color archetypes
rubrics_metrics.description: Blonde jokes often place the blonde in relation to a brunette or redhead, using contrast to frame the punch line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This contrast reinforces an in-group/out-group dynamic (blonde vs. brunette/redhead) and is a common structural device for producing the humor in the cycle.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meta-jokes about blonde jokes
rubrics_metrics.description: A class of meta-jokes exists in which a blonde complains about the stereotype propagated by blonde jokes, but the punch line then actually reinforces the stereotype (i.e., jokes about the jokes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meta-jokes commonly use irony: the blonde's attempt to denounce stereotyping becomes the setup for a stereotypical punch line. The ventriloquist example on the page illustrates this pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variants and related subtypes (sorority/Essex girl etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Many blonde jokes are rephrased sorority-girl or Essex-girl jokes; the British 'Essex girl' joke is very similar and satirises working-class girls from Essex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize parallel joke cycles in other cultures/groups (e.g., redneck jokes, ethnic jokes) — variants change wording and target but keep the same structural stereotype-based humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical continuity of stereotype-based jokes
rubrics_metrics.description: Jokes about stereotypically stupid people have circulated since the seventeenth century with only the wording and targeted groups changed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this to contextualize the blonde joke cycle as one instantiation of a long-standing folk practice of targeting perceived low intelligence in a group for humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criticism: offensiveness and sexism
rubrics_metrics.description: Like all humour based on stereotypes, blonde jokes are considered offensive to many people, particularly blonde women. They have been criticized as sexist because the target is invariably dimwitted, female and sexually promiscuous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scholarly criticism and empirical studies (cited) note that such jokes perpetuate gender discrimination and ambivalent sexism; producers/consumers should be aware of the discriminatory effects and social consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social function: rivalry and derision
rubrics_metrics.description: Blonde jokes serve as a form of blonde versus brunette rivalry and function socially to deride or marginalize the target group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understand jokes' role in group identity and social hierarchy — they can reinforce social boundaries and negative beliefs about the target group.
